doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: What Gallodoro is doing now
summary: Gallodoro plays trios and quartets and describes standing ovations at a Saratoga coffee house; Rowe notes the lasting power of classic music.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well you guys are staying active these days.
Tell me what you’re up to these days.
Oh, I do trios, quartets, duos, you know.
I just played in Saratoga at Nina’s Coffee House.
Oh, I’ve heard of this place.

I played there twice. Now this is the truth, I don’t brag. We packed them in, standing ovation. Eight months ago the same thing. So I asked the lady, I says, “Tell me, does everybody get that?” “No, only one other group gets a standing ovation, but I don’t remember who it was.” She says, otherwise you do.
Well there’s something to be said for the classic music of that day. It has lasted.
